chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sanadi ibn Muhammad, from al-Saffan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'My father and mother be sacrificed for you, I have made it incumbent upon myself to walk to the House of God.' He said: 'Expiate your oath, for you have only made an oath upon yourself, and what you made for God, fulfill it.'

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي: I made it incumbent upon myself (vow/nadhr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow to walk to the Kaaba and how is its expiation determined?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between a vow (nadhr) and an oath (yamin) based on the explicit dedication to God, ruling that a vow to walk to the Kaaba without such dedication is treated as a personal oath requiring expiation. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the linguistic formulation determines the legal category, aligning with the broader tradition where 'nadhr' implies a binding commitment to God while 'yamin' is a personal pledge. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on oaths, emphasizing that the intent and wording dictate whether one fulfills the act or pays kaffarah.
